newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian army chief named information minister.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian army chief named information minister.

text.p: Indonesia's retiring army chief of staff General Hartono was named information minister on Friday in a surprise move, replacing veteran politician and chairman of President Suharto's ruling Golkar party, Harmoko.
State Secretary Murdiono said Harmoko, who led Golkar to sweep more than 74 percent of the vote in last week's general elections, will be minister for special affairs and retain his party post.
"General Hartono will be appointed information minister as the army chief of staff will this month be of an age when, according to the rules, he must retire," he said.
Hartono reached the mandatory retirement age last year but was given a one-year extension by Suharto. He will be 56 next Tuesday.
Indonesian officers generally go into business or government after retiring.

Murdiono said the commander of the army's strategic reserve (Kostrad), Lieutenant-General Wiranto, would take over as the new chief of staff. Wiranto in turn will be replaced at Kostrad by Major-General Sugiono, currently commander of the presidential guard.
Murdiono brushed aside speculation that the move could be part of a wider cabinet reshuffle.
"I don't like to say that because only Harmoko's position has been changed. Usually a reshuffle will cover many ministers," he said.
Murdiono said more details on Harmoko's newly-created portfolio would be announced later, adding Hartono would be installed at an official ceremony next Wednesday.
Harmoko has served as information minister for about 14 years and has been a member of Suharto's last three cabinets.
A former journalist who founded the popular Pos Kota newspaper, he is widely expected to be appointed speaker of parliament and head of the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR).
The MPR, comprising the 500 members of parliament and 500 appointees, elects the president and vice-president every five years.

Suharto, who is 76 on Sunday, is widely expected to run for a seventh five-year term at the MPR meeting in March next year. There is keen interest in who he will select as vice-president -- and potential successor, given his age.

Diplomatic analysts said that over the coming months, Suharto would seek to build a consensus within the powerful military and political elite, particularly for his vice-presidential choice as his own election would be assured.
